context: Request: the highest-value financing the firm has closed, to lead pitch credentials. Rubric: 1005-00001 (Nexford Industrial, $1.4B senior secured term loan B) identified as the highest; precision allows 1005-00001 or 1041-00003 (Solara/Cloudium acquisition, $3.74B term loan B in a merger matter).

stages.stage: Search within a candidate matter's files

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: declared: Read documents picked from the file listing. Reads eight documents of three leading candidates (credit agreements, commitment letter, funds flow, closing memo), lists the top candidate's closing files and reads two more of its documents. The review flags two comparison matters left unopened.

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: declared: Read documents picked from the file listing (attempt 2). Reads four documents of two more candidates; one path fails.

stages.stage: Write the response
stages.note: Writes an acquisition-related debt package from a merger matter as the largest closed financing, with the dedicated term-loan matters as smaller comparisons. The review flags the committed-versus-funded figure and asks to confirm the client role.

stages.stage: Check or revise the response
stages.note: Re-reads the response, checks cited paths and makes two edits scoping the ranking to the matters reviewed.

stages.stage: Check or revise the response
stages.note: Attempt 2: re-reads seven cited documents; no edit.

stages.stage: Finish the run
stages.note: Calls finish.

runs.failure_point: The answer leads with an acquisition-related debt package from a merger matter and names the dedicated term-loan matter only as a smaller comparison.

first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) The review closing the last reading stage told the agent to lead with the acquisition package and name the term-loan matter as the comparison, and the answer did so.

divergence: All three runs fail the same way at the write stage. Each surfaced both matters through path sweeps and amount scans, read the term-loan matter's agreement and the acquisition matter's credit agreement and funds flow, and led the answer with the larger acquisition debt package, listing the term-loan matter as a smaller comparison. T1 also paired the parallel read results with other paths and gave the term-loan matter a small revolver amount, which two reviews flagged and the edits did not fix. No review questioned counting the acquisition package as the firm's own closed financing; in T2 the last reading review recommended leading with it.
